newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: 500 PNG villagers flee homes fearing cyanide poison.
newsitem.headline: 500 PNG villagers flee homes fearing cyanide poison.

text.p: More than 500 Papua New Guineans are abandoning their village fearing an old gold mine tailings dam on Mount Victor in the Eastern Highlands is leaking cyanide into a river which runs by their village.
"We are taking no chances. Our people live in the place and are going to a safer place uphill," Tau Boga, villager and Goroka provincial government official, told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We have noticed that the river has become discoloured and that the surface has a filmy substance similar to an oil discharge," Boga said.
Boga said most of the 500-plus inhabitants of Saiyori village should have evacuated the village, 1.5 kms (one mile) from the gold mine, by the end of the week.
Initially the villagers will stay in neighbouring villages until the provincial government erects a tent village further up the mountain and nearer to the abandoned gold mine, said Boga.
The Mount Victor gold mine was closed in 1990 by its owner and operator Nuigini Mining Ltd.
The PNG Chamber of Mines and Petroleum said last week that the Mount Victor gold mine was decommissioned under strict environmental standards.

"The residual cyanide in the tailings dam water was detoxified before the water was discharged into a nearby stream, without any risk to downstream water supplies," said the chamber's executive director Greg Anderson.
"Thw whole mine site was then completely rehabilitated, including extensive forestation," Anderson said in a statement.
Anderson said tests last November of water samples at the mine site and nearby streams found no evidence of cyanide.
